body.statement:
For every fixed member of \(\mathfrak M\), do its exact risks establish both premises of \(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\text{-}grid\text{-}argmin\text{-}transfer}\) with the candidate functions \(A\) and \(B\)?  Concretely, can one prove the compact-window limit
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal M_n\\ a\leq m/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)
-\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}
\left\{A(\beta)m/\sqrt n+B(\beta)\sqrt n/m\right\}\right|
\longrightarrow0
\]
for every \(0<a<b<\infty\), together with sequential coercivity for bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\)?  Positive pilot fractions for which both waves retain nonvanishing fractions, and the case \(N=o(n)\), are proved by the two branches of \(\mathrm{lem{:}pilot\text{-}endpoint\text{-}exclusion}\).  The three remaining endpoint comparisons and the compact-window limit require the finite-boundary comparison and the pilot-information-to-action bridge.
body.justification: This question is the honest headline status of sharp pilot sizing.
body.gap: Compact-window second-order convergence and three endpoint lower comparisons remain unresolved.
body.consumer: No preregistered square-root pilot recommendation is certified until this question is answered.

obligation.what_is_open: The compact-window second-order risk approximation and sequential coercivity for bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).
obligation.obstruction: The exact risk identity contains only the deletion and action-loss components, but the frozen primitives do not control either component uniformly at the \(n^{-3/2}\) scale. The first-order oracle-gain theorem supplies only an \(o(n^{-1})\) remainder, the pilot-information audit prevents replacing the realized pilot information by \(I(\beta)\), and the unresolved finite-boundary comparison is needed to rule out second-order tie and unequal-inclusion corrections.
obligation.attempted: Reused the exact two-component identity, the first-order oracle-gain expansion, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, both proved macroscopic exclusions, and the conditional deterministic balanced-grid transfer. These results isolate but do not prove the finite-boundary and information-to-action comparisons required at frontier scale.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact identity
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
=D_{n,m}(\beta)+L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
\]
and the conditional deterministic balanced-grid transfer are proved.  Uniformly for \(m/\sqrt n\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\), the missing compact-window premise reduces to the coefficient-level comparisons
\[
D_{n,m}(\beta)
=A(\beta)\frac{m}{n^2}+o(n^{-3/2}),
\qquad
L_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)
=\frac{B(\beta)}{nm}+o(n^{-3/2}),
\]
together with the matching arbitrary-rule lower comparison.  The two branches of \(\mathrm{lem{:}pilot\text{-}endpoint\text{-}exclusion}\) prove coercivity when \(N=o(n)\) and when both waves retain nonvanishing fractions.  The only unresolved boundary regimes are bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).  Neither coefficient-level expansion follows from the proved first-order oracle gain.
